Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are already out in the middle now. Sophia Dunkley and Alice Capsey are the two openers for England Women. Arundhati Reddy to start proceedings with the ball. Also, Richa Ghosh, the keeper, is standing up to the stumps. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

England lose grip after dream start - England Women will be slightly disappointed with their bowling and fielding effort after making the perfect start through Lauren Bell’s double strike in the opening over. However, Wong’s expensive 27-run over shifted the momentum completely as India counter-attacked strongly through Yastika Bhatia and Jemimah Rodrigues. England struggled to create chances for most of the innings before Yastika’s run out in the 14th over sparked a mini-collapse. Charlie Dean was excellent with figures of 1/26, while debutant Tilly Corteen-Coleman also impressed with 1/19 (3). Lauren Bell was still the standout bowler with a fine three-wicket haul, but England’s batters now face a stiff challenge if they are to continue their strong record at this venue.

From early shock to strong finish - India Women suffered an early blow, losing both Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma in the very first over. But Yastika Bhatia and Jemimah Rodrigues responded in stunning fashion, taking the attack to England and powering India to 72 in the Powerplay, their highest against England in this format. Both batters smashed impressive fifties while adding a brilliant 126-run stand in just 76 balls. England hit back strongly though, removing both in the same over as India slipped from 133/2 to 148/6. Deepti Sharma’s handy 22 off 13 balls late in the innings ensured India still finished close to the 190-run mark.

Yastika-Jemimah counterpunch lifts India - Well, that was quite a rollercoaster of an innings. England made the perfect start with Lauren Bell striking early, but India responded brilliantly through Yastika Bhatia and Jemimah Rodrigues, who counter-attacked with intent and shifted the momentum. The hosts clawed their way back during the middle overs with a much-improved bowling effort to pull the game back into the balance. However, India will head into the break as the happier side after finishing strongly, smashing 27 runs off the final two overs.

A hasty single to wrap a very, very chaotic first inning. Slower ball, full at the stumps. Gaud reads it early, drops it softly to Bell's left and scurries through for a quick single. The bowler rushes across and picks the ball before throwing at the non-striker's end, but misses her shy. So 10 runs off the final over. INDIA FINISH AT 188/7.

OUT! TAKEN SPECTACULARLY! A special moment for the youngster as Tilly Corteen-Coleman grabs her first-ever T20I wicket. She is over the moon and why not? That was the pressure created from Corteen-Coleman. Four singles in the over and a dot ball as well. Ghosh thought she had to find the boundary. Length ball around the fourth stump, and Richa has premeditated this completely. Changes her stance and goes for the reverse sweep, only to get herself in a tangle. Top edges it and the ball balloons over Wong at short third. She turns around, sprints towards the fence, keeps her eyes locked on the ball the entire way, and stretches out both hands in front to take a fabulous catch. India Women are 148/5, 4 overs left.

Yastika Bhatia has notched up a superb 31-ball fifty, while Jemimah Rodrigues is not too far away. The duo is playing aggressively and have put the hosts under a lot of pressure. Lauren Bell's double-wicket opening over looks very distant now, as England Women need wickets to get back in this game. They did manage a couple of quiet overs, but the momentum is with the visitors here. Danielle Gibson will bowl after the break.

Commentary.Commentary: Not many would have thought India Women would finish this as their best Powerplay against England in WT20Is (as mentioned by Nick Knight on air), after losing both the openers in the first over. Yastika Bhatia has been simply superb, while Jemimah Rodrigues is also playing a good hand, but the 27-run over from Issy Wong is what shifted the momentum completely, and the hosts are desperate to break this stand, which is growing and proving to be match-defining here. Also, Danielle Gibson to bowl after the break.
Flat and full, on the stumps. Jemimah Rodrigues leans and pushes it to the right of the bowler for a single. India Women are 73/2 at the end of the Powerplay.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Charlie Dean to Jemimah Rodrigues, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length on leg at 82 kph, and Jemimah goes for the pull. Gets a top edge that balloons behind her. Corteen-Coleman charges in from short fine leg but never quite gets under it, stretching out her right hand without making contact. Two leg byes taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Charlie Dean to Jemimah Rodrigues, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Flights it full and turns it on the pads. Jemimah Rodrigues clips it to short fine leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Charlie Dean to Jemimah Rodrigues, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Excellent shot! A real drag-downer, on the leg stump. Jemimah Rodrigues shuffles a bit and pulls it over backward square leg for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Charlie Dean to Jemimah Rodrigues, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Just short! On a length on the off stump. Jemimah is a bit too early into the shot and chips it to the left of the bowler but it falls just short of Dean who dives to her left.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Charlie Dean to Jemimah Rodrigues, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Rodrigues shuffles outside off and Dean follows the batter. Jemimah takes it on the full and eases it to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Charlie Dean to Jemimah Rodrigues, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: The captain, Charlie Dean, brings herself into the attack now. She replaces Tilly Corteen-Coleman.
Slows it up, full and on off, Yastika Bhatia drills it towards mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Sophie Ecclestone to Yastika Bhatia, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! More runs! Quicker delivery, full but down the leg side. Yastika Bhatia gets down on one knee and sweeps it behind square on the leg side four more runs. 15 runs off Sophie's first over!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Sophie Ecclestone to Yastika Bhatia, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! That is a top shot! Sophie Ecclestone gives this one some more air, full and on middle. Yastika Bhatia skips down the track to get to the pitch of it and tonks it over the long on fence for a biggie. This is also brings up the 50-RUN stand between these two batters in double quick time.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Sophie Ecclestone to Yastika Bhatia, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Too full, on middle and leg. Jemimah mistimes her sweep shot to the right of square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Sophie Ecclestone to Jemimah Rodrigues, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Flighted, full and on off, Jemimah Rodrigues pushes it off the bottom part of the bat back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Sophie Ecclestone to Jemimah Rodrigues, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Gets greeted with a boundary! Tossed up, full and on middle, Jemimah Rodrigues uses backs away to go inside-out and carasses the drive through extra covers for four runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Sophie Ecclestone to Jemimah Rodrigues, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: India are in command right now and England need a breakthrough to stop this run flow. For that, Dean brings her trump card. Sophie Ecclestone, with 143 T20I wickets, is into the attack now. She replaces Lauren Bell.
Tossed up outside off, Yastika steps out and mistimes the drive to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Tilly Corteen-Coleman to Yastika Bhatia, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Beautifully played! Dropped full and sliding into the batter, Yastika Bhatia sits down on a knee and nails the sweep shot, to the left of the diving fielder at backward square leg for a boundary. 50 UP FOR INDIA! In just 3.5 overs and despite losing the openers in the first over itself.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Tilly Corteen-Coleman to Yastika Bhatia, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Another full toss, drifting on leg. Jemimah Rodrigues advances a little and chips it over mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Tilly Corteen-Coleman to Jemimah Rodrigues, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Floated, full and on middle, Yastika Bhatia clips it through mid-wicket for a run.

Commentary.Commentary: Will Wong continue? Nope. It is the debutant who will roll her arm over. It's always a big moment for any player to represent the nation for the first time. It brings a bit of nerves. Let's see how she deals with it. Here's Tilly Corteen-Coleman into the attack. She replaces Issy Wong.
Lovely bowling! Short of a length and around off, angling it away from the batter, Yastika Bhatia tries to play from the crease but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Lauren Bell to Yastika Bhatia, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! The runs just keep flowing! Lauren Bell hits the deck hard from over the wicket, on off, gets it to nip back in. Yastika Bhatia pushes at it with hard hands and gets an inside edge past the stumps and to the fine leg fence for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Lauren Bell to Yastika Bhatia, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Halt. A concussion test is underway for Yastika Bhatia as she copped a blow on her helmet. Dean threw it wayward to the batting end and it struck Bhatia's helmet instead. Yastika is in looking alright as she has a chat with the physio.

Pitched up and on middle, Jemimah Rodrigues steps across and tucks it towards mid-wicket for a single. Charlie Dean picks up the ball and throws it at the batter's end, where the ball crashes onto the top of Bhatia's helmet. Ouch!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Lauren Bell to Jemimah Rodrigues, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Just up and over! Bell goes for a fuller delivery, but Jemimah Rodrigues walks out of the crease and converts it into a full toss. Uses her wrists and flicks it over short mid-wicket for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Lauren Bell to Jemimah Rodrigues, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Full again and on off, shaping away this time, Jemimah Rodrigues strides out and pushes it to short cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Lauren Bell to Jemimah Rodrigues, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Touch fuller and around off, shaping in a bit, Jemimah Rodrigues looks to drive it away but gets beaten on the inside edge.

FOUR! Finishes the over with a boundary as well! A juicy full toss, outside off. Yastika Bhatia presses in front and creams it through cover and point for a cracking boundary.

Commentary.Commentary: Just like that, both the Indian openers are dismissed. England right on top and are pumped up. Jemimah Rodrigues is in at number 4. Issy Wong will bowl from the other end.

OUT! TAKEN! Lauren Bell is on fire here. She removes both the Indian openers in the very first over. This is full again and on middle, angling into the leg side. Shafali Verma backs away and tries to lift it over mid on, but gets cramped up for room. She ends up lobbing it tamely off the inside half of her bat towards mid on, where Alice Capsey dives forward and takes a good low catch. India in early trouble.

Commentary.Commentary: That's some way to get underway. Bell trumps Mandhana in the battle of the two heavyweights. Perfect start for England. Yastika Bhatia is the new batter in at number 3.

OUT! CAUGHT! Wow, now that's what you call a perfect start. It does not get better than this for England Women. Lauren Bell starts with a full delivery and around off. Smriti Mandhana looks to drive it on the up but the ball just holds up on the surface and she cannot keep her shot down. It flies towards short cover, where Charlie Dean leaps up and takes a fine catch above her head. A golden duck for Mandhana and India Women are 0/1.
Commentary.Howout: c Charlie Dean b Lauren Bell
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Lauren Bell to Smriti Mandhana, OUT! c Charlie Dean b Lauren Bell.

Commentary.Commentary: All set to get a fresh series underway. It's a beautiful evening in Chelmsford and the conditions are a bit overcast, but no rain threat at all. The English players are in a huddle near the pitch before they spread out. Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana are the two Indian openers who walk to the crease. Mandhana will take the strike. Lauren Bell has the new ball. A slip in place and here we go...

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana (C), Shafali Verma, Yastika Bhatia, Jemimah Rodrigues, Bharti Fulmali, Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Arundhati Reddy, Sree Charani, Nandni Sharma, Kranti Gaud.

England Women (Playing XI) - Sophia Dunkley, Alice Capsey, Amy Jones (WK), Heather Knight, Freya Kemp, Danielle Gibson, Charlie Dean (C), Issy Wong, Sophie Ecclestone, Lauren Bell, Tilly Corteen-Coleman (On T20I debut).
TOSS - England Women have won the toss and elected to BOWL first.

Last chance to find the right balance - India Women arrive in England as the reigning 50-over world champions, but a T20 World Cup crown remains elusive. This series offers the final opportunity to settle lingering questions, particularly around the lower middle-order and bowling attack. Smriti Mandhana, still only 29 and already the second-highest run-scorer in T20I history, will be central to India's plans. Captain Harmanpreet Kaur is just nine runs away from becoming the third woman to 4,000 runs in T20Is. The bowling unit, however, remains a work in progress. Uncapped seamer Nandni Sharma, the joint-leading wicket-taker at the most recent WPL and the first Indian bowler to claim a hat-trick in the competition has been included, though whether she debuts remains uncertain. Radha Yadav returns to add spin depth alongside Deepti Sharma, while Shafali Verma's 25-ball fifty in a warm-up game here two days ago suggests the batters are already in rhythm. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

New era, familiar expectations - England Women walk into this series with a clear mission - find the right combinations before the World Cup on home soil. The absence of captain Nat Sciver-Brunt through injury is a significant blow, though she is expected to return for the global tournament. In her place, Charlie Dean will lead a side that features a new-look opening pair of Sophia Dunkley and Alice Capsey, both eager to stake their claim. All eyes will also be on Sophie Ecclestone, once the No. 1 ranked T20I bowler who is closing in on becoming only the fourth woman to 150 wickets in the format. With Danielle Gibson and Freya Kemp adding all-round depth, and the small boundaries of Chelmsford inviting aggressive batting, England will back themselves to extend their remarkable home record.

World Cup rehearsal - The County Ground in Chelmsford, fondly known as England's fortress prepares to host the opening salvo of a series that means more than just bilateral silverware. With the Women's T20 World Cup just two weeks away, England Women and India Women lock horns in the first of three T20Is, each looking to fine-tune their combinations before the global showpiece begins next month. England have won 12 of their 14 T20Is at this venue, including eight-wicket victories over India in 2012 and 2021. India, however, arrive with the confidence of having secured their first-ever bilateral T20I series win on English soil just last summer, a 3-2 triumph that announced them as genuine contenders.
... MATCH DAY ...

Final tune-up before the World Cup - With less than three weeks left for the Women's T20 World Cup to kick off in England and Wales, the teams are in the final stretch of their preparations for the showpiece event. Two heavyweights are all set to lock horns in a three-match series as they build up to that event. First up, England and India will meet in Chelmsford, before Bristol and then Taunton, with games 1 and 3 being evening fixtures while the second game will be an afternoon affair. Rivals set for another chapter - For the second time in under a year, India are touring England, and they carry plenty of happy memories from their last visit, where Harmanpreet Kaur and Co. clinched both the ODI and T20I series. Post the World Cup, these two sides are also scheduled to meet in a one-off Test at the iconic Lord's Cricket Ground. Final audition before the big stage - England's 2026 has been defined almost entirely by the New Zealand series, which they recently won 2-1, and it was their first T20I action since July last year. Ahead of that series, though, they held an extensive selection camp in Pretoria, South Africa, where a 30-member group was split into two squads of 15 for a five-match intra-squad series to help finalise their World Cup squad. Navigating the absences - The hosts come into this series carrying a significant cloud over them. Captain Nat Sciver-Brunt is still recovering from a calf tear and, having missed the New Zealand series, she will also sit out the India series with the hope that she will be fit in time for the World Cup. Danni Wyatt-Hodge, meanwhile, welcomed her daughter recently and will be available for the final two matches. With Wyatt-Hodge absent during the New Zealand series, Alice Capsey was promoted to open, and she seized the opportunity brilliantly. Sophia Dunkley is another exciting batter up top, while Heather Knight, with her ability to tackle spin through her sweeps and reverse sweeps, will be key to addressing India's spin challenge. Maia Bouchier has been drafted into the squad to cover Wyatt-Hodge's absence, and although she is not in the World Cup squad, she will be keen to make a case for herself should an injury create an opportunity at the eleventh hour. Varied bowling attack - Freya Kemp and Dani Gibson provide batting depth to go with their bowling credentials, with Gibson starring in the series decider against New Zealand, where England skittled the White Ferns out for 80, picking up a three-wicket haul in the process. Lauren Bell will lead the pace attack, while Lauren Filer and Issy Wong are pacers cut from the same cloth with the express pace they bring, though the tall Filer also extracts extra bounce to trouble batters. In the absence of Sciver-Brunt, England will be led by Charlie Dean, with Sophie Ecclestone, Linsey Smith and 18-year-old Tilly Corteen-Coleman also part of the spin attack. Corteen-Coleman is a product of England's Under-19 setup and is yet to make her senior T20I debut. Searching for answers - India have endured a mixed run of results in 2026. In February, they pulled off a landmark series win in Australia, their first there in a decade, but they then toured South Africa in April and suffered a chastening 4-1 T20I series defeat at the hands of Laura Wolvaardt's team, which left some questions hanging over their T20 game ahead of the World Cup. Openers must fire - The batting for the tourists largely revolves around the top four of Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues and skipper Harmanpreet Kaur. When the openers provide strong starts, it allows Jemimah and Harmanpreet to bat with far greater freedom through the middle overs. Bharti Fulmali and Richa Ghosh bring explosiveness in the lower order, while Deepti Sharma and Shreyanka Patil offer the ability to contribute in both departments. There is also a welcome return for left-handed wicketkeeper batter Yastika Bhatia, who finds her way back into the setup after a long and frustrating run with injuries. Bowling options in focus - Renuka Singh Thakur will be key with her ability to make the new ball talk in English conditions, with Arundhati Reddy, Kranti Gaud and Nandni Sharma as her supporting pace options. Nandni comes into the squad on the back of a stellar WPL campaign, finishing as the joint-leading wicket-taker of the tournament to earn a maiden India call-up. Apart from Deepti and Shreyanka, Sree Charani and Radha Yadav are the other spin-bowling options skipper Harmanpreet will have at her disposal. Form (Last 5 completed matches, recent first) - ENG - WLWWL | IND - LWLLL. What to expect? The County Ground in Chelmsford has generally produced good batting surfaces over the years, and India would have taken plenty of confidence from the recent tour game where they piled on 200 against the England Development XI at the same venue. That outing should also have given them a useful read of the conditions ahead of the series opener. With both sides packed with power, depth and plenty of match-winners, this series promises to be a compelling contest between two teams still searching for the perfect balance ahead of the World Cup. All the ingredients are in place for a cracking series opener in Chelmsford.
